newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong farewell to empire details unveiled.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong farewell to empire details unveiled.

text.p: Britain's end of empire bash in Hong Kong may be the biggest, the splashiest and, possibly, the most tearful farewell party ever thrown.
The guest list runs to 10,000 names, topped by Prince Charles, according to details announced on Saturday.
For entertainment, there will be dragon dancers, two 70-piece orchestras, military bands, a massed choir of 650 adults and children, poetry reading and bagpipes.
An estimated 100 million television viewers will watch the Union Jack and Hong Kong flags lowered at sunset.
The emotional ceremony will be held against the spectacular backdrop of Victoria Harbour.

Six choreographers, 12 stage managers and no fewer than 150 technicians are putting the finishing touches to the June 30 spectacular at East Tamar, site of the former Royal Navy headquarters in Hong Kong.
Some 300 tonnes of equipment has been shipped from Britain, Australia, Canada and Singapore for a night of colour, pageantry, music and dance.
When the 15 km (9.4 miles) of power cable has been laid, and everything is plugged in, the sound systems and lighting towers will use enough electricity to power 500 apartments.
The price tag for Britain's emotional farewell to its last major colony: roughly $3 million, all paid for by the British government.
Much of that is being handed to the New York-based event company, Caribiner International Inc, whose previous triumphs have included the much-hyped launch of Microsoft's Windows 95 software product.
Raymond Wong, one of the official organisers, told reporters the show "is designed to express the gratitude of Britain to the people of Hong Kong".
Joining VIPs, including Governor Chris Patten, on the stands will be 2,200 ordinary Hong Kong citizens, chosen at random in a computer ballot, and 1,000 journalists.

Two vast stages have been erected on the edge of a concrete square, which until a few years ago was a mooring basin for small naval craft. The best view, though, will be had from windows of the Bank of America Tower and Lippo building, which overlook the area.
Another vantage point will be the Prince of Wales Barracks, soon to be renamed as the headquarters of China's People's Liberation Army.
On the night itself, the royal yacht Britannia will be berthed just behind the twin stages.

After the show, Charles and Patten will join Chinese President Jiang Zemin, new Hong Kong chief executive Tung Chee-hwa and British Prime Minister Tony Blair for the final handover ceremony at midnight at the nearby Hong Kong Convention Centre.
Shortly after, the governor and Charles will board the Britannia and sail away into the darkness.
